title: Shema Yisrael
hookLine: read the Shema's first two words in Hebrew

cards: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." Up to now on this path, you've met that line in English.
In Deuteronomy, the next verse says to speak these words when you sit in your house and walk by the way, when you lie down and when you rise up.
So it's said at bedtime and in the morning service, and tradition places it on the lips of children and of the dying. In the prayer book it stands in Hebrew, and it opens with two words.
Today they stop being sounds and become letters you can read.

teach.h: SHEMA: SH, MA, AND A SILENT EYE.
teach.b: Shema Yisrael. Read it four ways. First, shema.
Right to left: shin, with its dot on the right arm, sh. Under it, two dots stacked, a mark that here barely sounds. Then mem, with a short line under it: ma.
Then ayin, the eye, which says nothing. Sh, ma, and silence: shema. It means hear, or listen.
Second, Yisrael. Yod, the small one, with a dot under it: yi. Then the three-armed letter again, but the dot has moved to the left arm.
That makes it sin, which says s. Yis. Then resh with the T-shaped mark: ra.
Then alef, silent, carrying two dots side by side: eh. Then lamed. Yis, ra, el.
Yisrael. Third, a detail in the scroll.
By scribal tradition, in a Torah scroll the ayin at the end of shema and the dalet at the end of the verse's last word are written larger than the letters around them.
Some readers notice that together they spell ed, a witness. That's a reading, not the verse's plain meaning, and it's offered as one. Fourth, a gesture.
The Talmud tells of Rabbi Judah the Prince passing his hand over his eyes as he said the Shema, and a custom grew from it: covering the eyes for the first line.
The eyes close. The ears open. It begins with listening.

how: Jews who keep the daily prayers say the Shema in the morning and evening prayers and again at bedtime, and a common custom is to cover the eyes with the right hand while saying the first line.

games.q: you're reading Yisrael and come to the three-armed letter. the dot sits on the left arm. what do you say?
games.why: s. the dot on the left makes it sin, so the word is yis-ra-el.

practice: Look at the two words on the screen and read them from the right, slowly: sh, ma, shema; yis, ra, el, Yisrael.
Then, if you like, cover your eyes the way the custom does, say them again from memory, and sit a breath or two behind your hand, listening. If you pray, you can say the whole first line.
